transcript:
Meeting Header
Date/Time: 2025-07-24 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 mins
Recorded by: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Chen (CTO, NeuroLine), Ravi Kumar (Lead ML Engineer), Olivia Park (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated; may be imperfect):
NeuroLine is evaluating Redwood for a hybrid hosting strategy — started with hosted API for pilot, but leaning toward Dedicated or Private for PHI workflows. Key concerns: p95 latency targets for streaming responses (<= 220ms for short prompts, <= 1s for 1k token streams), sustained token/sec throughput, burst concurrency, and security (SOC2, SSO, KMS, data residency). They will share traces and run a benchmark pilot with Redwood's SE. Next steps agreed: benchmark run, share security docs, send draft pilot SOW.

Topics:
- Hosting mode tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
- p95 streaming latency targets and token/sec benchmarks
- Concurrency, cold starts, KV cache and batching strategies
- Security/compliance: SOC2, ISO, SSO, KMS, VPC
- Pilot scope and timeline

Action items (auto):
- Lena to send pricing + latency spreadsheet
- Samir to define bench plan and env reqs
- NeuroLine to provide sample traces and seqlen distribution

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick off, um, quick intro from our side. I'm Lena, AE at Redwood, and Samir is our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Hi all. Quick note, if audio drops we can hop to chat. We'll try to be crisp — want to understand your p ninety five targets and typical bursts.
[00:34] Dr. Maya Chen: Thanks. For context, NeuroLine processes clinical notes for triage — most calls are short two to three sentence prompts but sometimes we stream long summaries ~800 to 1,200 tokens. We're targeting p95 under 250 ms for short queries and under one second p95 for streaming 1k token responses end-to-end.
[01:05] Ravi Kumar: To add, our current infra is on AWS EKS with GPUs in prod, using a rabbitmq fronting. Right now we're seeing high variance with our in-house endpoint — p95 spikes to 1.6s during bursts.
[01:29] Olivia Park: Security is a hard constraint — PHI, so we need KMS HSM integration, audit logs, and either VPC private deploy or Dedicated with customer VPC peering. Data residency EU-first.
[01:50] Lena Ortiz: Got it. That aligns with other healthcare customers. Quick question on scale, what's your steady-state qps and burst concurrency?
[02:04] Ravi Kumar: Steady is around 15 qps with mostly short queries, bursts up to 600 concurrent requests during overnight batch triage windows, and spikes for experiments. Token/sec wise, we estimate 40k tokens/s sustained across fleet during peak — but that's rough.
[02:33] Samir Patel: Helpful. For those numbers, we typically look at a Dedicated pool for predictable throughput and Private for full control. Hosted can work for pilot but for PHI/DPA reasons many go Dedicated or Private. Also caching — prefix / K V cache — reduces token work for repeated prompts.
[02:58] Dr. Maya Chen: What's the expected cold-start behavior for streaming? We saw big tail latencies during cold starts on other runtimes.
[03:12] Samir Patel: Cold starts are influenced by model size, quantization, and kernel warm-up. Our runtime keeps a warm pool for canary capacity; for p95 streaming we aim to keep p95 cold under 500ms extra, but depends on sequence length. Also we do continuous batching so small queries can piggyback but that trades latency.
[03:38] Ravi Kumar: Can you talk about token/sec benchmarks — like how many short prompts per GPU and streaming token throughput per GPU? We need numbers to compare to our in-house tests.
[03:52] Samir Patel: Sure. Ballpark, for a 70B quantized model on A100-class GPUs in our Dedicated config you might see ~350 tokens/sec per GPU for heavy autoregressive tasks, higher for streaming-friendly models and with KV cache. With batching across clients and async prefixes, the effective tokens/sec can go to thousands per GPU — but depends a lot on seqlen distribution.
[04:19] Olivia Park: That variability is our concern, we need predictable p95s. Do you provide SLOs for latency on Dedicated? And what about SLAs for Hosted?
[04:31] Lena Ortiz: Dedicated carries SLA-backed throughput and latency targets — we work with customers to profile their workload and allocate capacity. Hosted has published median/percentile benchmarks, but enterprise customers usually reserve Dedicated capacity for p95 guarantees.
[04:48] Dr. Maya Chen: We also need to validate psychometric stability — i.e., the model's outputs don't regress when quantized or batched. How do you guard quality vs quantization and batching?
[05:02] Samir Patel: We run evals tied to your prompt suite — Redwood Optimize recommends quant profiles and runs regression alerts. For pilot we'll include a small eval set to monitor quality drift. Also can do A/B rollouts and automatic fallback to FP16 variants if quality drops.
[05:22] Ravi Kumar: For the benchmark, we'll provide a capture of real traffic — headers, average prompt seqlen, distribution of token lengths. Is that enough for you to size?
[05:33] Samir Patel: Yes — that's ideal. Please send a 24h trace and we'll map seq len percentiles and token/sec expectations.
[05:45] Lena Ortiz: Timeline question: you mentioned pilot next month — what's your procurement timeline and who are stakeholders?
[05:52] Dr. Maya Chen: Procurement and security review in mid-August, budget sign-off in Sept. Stakeholders: myself, VP Eng (not on call), legal, and infra lead Olivia.
[06:07] Olivia Park: We'll need SOC2 Type II report, ISO certs, and a network diagram for VPC/private deployment. Also SSO via SAML and RBAC for platform access.
[06:20] Lena Ortiz: Sounds straightforward. We'll send SOC2/ISO and SSO integration docs. For VPC private option we have an on-prem package and a VPC appliance; both support KMS and HSM integrations.
[06:34] Ravi Kumar: On encryption — we need BYOK with HSM. Can Redwood support customer-managed keys and key rotation policies?
[06:43] Samir Patel: Yes, Private and Dedicated support customer KMS/HSM. Hosted supports customer-managed keys via our KMS integration in certain enterprise plans; we'll note constraints in the security docs.
[06:58] Dr. Maya Chen: One more on fallbacks — if Dedicated pool saturates during spike, what's the auto-fallback behaviour?
[07:08] Samir Patel: We route by policy — your requests can fallback to a lower-cost model variant or other region with capacity. You can set SLOs where we prefer latency-first or cost-first fallback. For PHI you'd probably prefer failover to Private nodes or queue with backpressure rather than cross-region spill.
[07:30] Ravi Kumar: Do you have telemetry at token-level so we can cost-allocate across teams?
[07:37] Lena Ortiz: Yes, Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. You can export to Datadog/CloudWatch.
[07:48] Olivia Park: Are audit logs tamper-evident and retained for 13 months? We have audit requirements.
[07:56] Samir Patel: We can configure retention; tamper-evidence via signed logs is available on Private deployments, and append-only audit logs for Dedicated.
[08:10] Dr. Maya Chen: Let's dig into the bench plan — what do you need from us to run a realistic token/sec test?
[08:19] Samir Patel: Ideally: (1) request traces with timestamps, (2) sample prompt/response pairs, (3) seqlen histogram, (4) desired p95 targets and acceptance criteria. We'll run steady-state and burst tests, both cold-start and warm, and measure token/sec, p95, and tail.
[08:36] Ravi Kumar: For the steady-state, we want to target simulating 600 concurrent short queries with 1k token streaming spikes. Can you simulate our message queue pattern?
[08:48] Samir Patel: Yes — we can reproduce queue-driven bursts. We'll also test KV cache benefits by replaying repeated prefixes.
[08:58] Lena Ortiz: We'll send an example bench plan and scheduling options. We usually recommend 2-4 hour bench slots for real traffic capture.
[09:08] Dr. Maya Chen: Budget question — if we move to Dedicated, what's the ballpark monthly commitment for the scale we discussed?
[09:16] Lena Ortiz: Ballpark, depending on model family and quant, Dedicated pools for your size historically land in the mid-five-figures to low six-figures per month; we'll send a tailored estimate after we map token/sec and desired p95s.
[09:32] Ravi Kumar: Any gotchas about streaming versus non-streaming throughput? We saw a vendor halve throughput when enabling chunked streaming.
[09:43] Samir Patel: Streaming introduces incremental overhead per chunk, but our runtime optimizes streaming paths. You can expect a modest throughput drop but better tail control because we pre-allocate sending pipelines. We'll quantify in bench results.
[09:58] Olivia Park: On compliance — are you able to support an audit where we run APT scans on the private nodes or host images?
[10:07] Samir Patel: For Private/on-prem we can accommodate security scans under NDA. For Dedicated we provide images and attestations; full host-level scans may have limits but we can discuss with security.
[10:21] Dr. Maya Chen: Ok. For next steps let's list specifics.
[10:27] Lena Ortiz: Recap — NeurosLine will: share traces (Ravi), sign NDA if needed for scans (Olivia), confirm bench windows. Redwood will: send security pack (Lena), bench plan (Samir), and pricing/estimate (Lena).
[10:45] Ravi Kumar: I'll send a 48h trace dump and seqlen histogram by Friday.
[10:51] Olivia Park: I'll coordinate with legal on NDA and SOC2 docs.
[10:56] Samir Patel: While you share traces, we'll spin up a dedicated bench harness and propose a 3-hour run. We'll include streaming and cold-start phases.
[11:07] Lena Ortiz: Great — I'll follow up by EOD Friday with the spreadsheet and SOW draft.
[11:14] Dr. Maya Chen: Thanks, appreciate the clarity. Looking forward to the bench results.
[11:20] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone — end.

Meeting ended.
